testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, a leak in one system:

options.text: Always means both systems are leaking.
May not affect the other system.
Will also affect the other system.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not affect the other system.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate brake systems. A leak in one system may not affect the other system.

questions.question: When carrying a sealed load, a driver should:

options.text: Open the load to check its safety.
Make sure the weight does not exceed legal limits.
Inspect inside the container before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the weight does not exceed legal limits.
questions.explanation: You cannot open a sealed load, but you must still check that the weight does not exceed legal limits.

questions.question: Distracted driving:

options.text: Only happens when you are doing something physical while driving.
Can happen from mental activities, like daydreaming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can happen from mental activities, like daydreaming.
questions.explanation: Distraction can be physical (like reaching for something), mental (like talking with a passenger), or both (like texting on a phone). To avoid distracted driving, pre-program radio stations, plan your route ahead, avoid difficult conversations while driving, adjust mirrors before leaving, and do not eat, drink, or smoke while driving.

questions.question: When starting a trip with cargo, the driver should:

options.text: Stop and check the cargo within the first 50 miles.
Drive faster than normal to test if the load is secure.
Only use side mirrors to check the cargo.
Not recheck cargo if it was secured before starting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and check the cargo within the first 50 miles.
questions.explanation: Check your cargo before starting your trip, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles after that.

questions.question: If you are convicted of a traffic violation (not parking), you must:

options.text: Put a sign on your vehicle about the conviction.
Give up your CDL for six months.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell your employer within 30 days.
questions.explanation: You must tell your employer about any traffic conviction within 30 days. You must also tell your motor vehicle licensing agency within 30 days if the conviction happened in another state. This rule does not apply to parking violations.

questions.question: A truck may need to stay below the legal maximum weight limit when driving:
questions.correctAnswerText: On a mountainous road.
questions.explanation: Under certain driving conditions, it is not safe to drive at the full legal maximum weight. Be careful in bad weather and on mountain roads.

questions.question: What is a Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR)?

options.text: The maximum loaded weight for a single vehicle as set by the manufacturer
The maximum weight a single vehicle can pull
The minimum weight a single vehicle can haul
The maximum weight that can be loaded on a trailer

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum loaded weight for a single vehicle as set by the manufacturer
questions.explanation: GVWR is the maximum weight set by the manufacturer for a vehicle and its load.

questions.question: Do not decide when to shift gears based on:

options.text: What other vehicles next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: What other vehicles next to you are doing.
questions.explanation: Shift gears based on your engine's rpm range. Shift up when your engine reaches the top of that range. You can also shift based on your speedometer and what gear works best at each speed.

questions.question: Most heavy trucks with manual transmissions require ____ to change gears.
questions.correctAnswerText: Double clutching
questions.explanation: Most heavy trucks with manual transmissions need double clutching to shift gears. This skill takes practice to master.

questions.question: Which surface has the least traction?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wet ice
questions.explanation: Be very careful when driving on melting ice. Wet ice is much more slippery than dry ice.

questions.question: What is the minimum number of tie-downs needed to secure a 10-foot piece of cargo?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two
questions.explanation: All cargo on flatbed trailers and trailers without sides must be tied down. Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. Always use at least two tie-downs, no matter the cargo size.

questions.question: When should you check cargo securement after starting a trip?
questions.correctAnswerText: After 50 miles
questions.explanation: Check cargo before you start, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles. The driver is responsible for keeping cargo safe and secure during the entire trip.

questions.question: What is Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW)?

options.text: The total weight of a vehicle and its cargo
The total weight of a vehicle without cargo
The total weight of cargo only
The maximum weight a vehicle is allowed to carry

questions.correctAnswerText: The total weight of a vehicle and its cargo
questions.explanation: Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW) is the combined weight of the vehicle itself plus all the cargo it is carrying.

questions.question: How do you check for a leak in hydraulic brakes?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal three times and hold it for five seconds. If the pedal moves, there may be a problem.
Push the brake pedal down and release it. If it does not return to normal position, there may be a problem.
Push the brake pedal down and release it. If it squeaks, there may be a problem.
Remove the rear wheel and listen for noise when the brake pedal is pressed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brake pedal three times and hold it for five seconds. If the pedal moves, there may be a problem.
questions.explanation: To check hydraulic brakes, pump the pedal three times, then press it firmly and hold for five seconds. The pedal should not move. If it does, you may have a leak or another problem in the brake system.

questions.question: Is a rear tire with 1/32 inch tread depth acceptable?
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Front tires must have at least 4/32 inch of tread depth. All other tires must have at least 2/32 inch of tread depth. A 1/32 inch tread is not acceptable.

questions.question: If you have an engine fire, what should you do?

options.text: Turn off the engine as soon as possible.
Do not use a fire extinguisher.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: To stop an engine fire from spreading, turn off the engine immediately. Do not open the hood unless you must.

questions.question: When entering traffic on an expressway during a skills test, you should:

options.text: Cut off other drivers if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for traffic.
questions.explanation: During the driving skills test, you may need to enter an expressway. Always check for traffic, use proper signals, and merge smoothly into the correct lane.

questions.question: What do air tank drains do?

options.text: Allow rain water to enter air tanks.
Remove water and oil from air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from air tanks.
questions.explanation: Air tanks have drains that remove water and compressor oil from the brake system. If water and oil build up, they can damage the air brake system.

questions.question: If your vehicle is hydroplaning, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle hydroplanes, do not brake. Instead, release the accelerator and push in the clutch. This will help you regain traction.

questions.question: What is true about dual tires?

options.text: They should not both touch the road surface.
They should not touch one another.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should not touch one another.
questions.explanation: When inspecting your vehicle, make sure your dual tires do not touch each other or any other part of the vehicle.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a distracted person that drivers should worry about?

options.text: A person talking to another person in their vehicle
A child on the side of the road
A construction worker on the side of the road
A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus

questions.correctAnswerText: A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
questions.explanation: Be careful near people who are not paying attention to traffic. Watch out for drivers talking to passengers, children near the road, and road workers.

questions.question: Rough acceleration is:

options.text: Not recommended because it can damage your vehicle.
Not recommended because it confuses other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not recommended because it can damage your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Speed up smoothly and gradually. Rough acceleration can cause jerking and mechanical damage to your vehicle.

questions.question: You should carry three red reflective triangles in your vehicle.
questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Your vehicle should have warning devices for when it breaks down. These can include three reflective triangles, six fuses, or three liquid burning flares.

questions.question: The service brake system:

options.text: Works when you press the brake pedal while driving normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Works when you press the brake pedal while driving normally.
questions.explanation: There are three separate braking systems: service brake, parking brake, and emergency brake. The service brake system activates when you use the brake pedal during normal driving.

questions.question: Very hot temperatures can cause:
questions.correctAnswerText: Tire failure.
questions.explanation: Heat causes air to expand, which increases tire pressure. High pressure can lead to tire failure. Check your tire pressure regularly in hot weather.

questions.question: Black ice is usually very thick.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it, which makes the road look wet instead of icy.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not stop, change gears, pass, or change lanes while crossing railroad tracks.

questions.question: A tired driver:

options.text: Is usually more careful than other drivers.
May be slower to make important decisions.

questions.correctAnswerText: May be slower to make important decisions.
questions.explanation: Tired drivers are slower to see hazards and react to them. Drowsy drivers cannot make quick, important decisions.

questions.question: Brakes that are out of adjustment will:

options.text: Cause some brakes to work too hard and fail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cause some brakes to work too hard and fail.
questions.explanation: Out-of-adjustment brakes wear out faster than properly adjusted brakes. Check your brakes often to prevent problems.

questions.question: If you see an aggressive driver crash ahead of you, you should:

options.text: Block the driver in with your vehicle.
Stop safely after the crash and tell police about the aggressive driving.
Pull over and yell at the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely after the crash and tell police about the aggressive driving.
questions.explanation: Stop a safe distance from the crash. Wait for police and report what you saw about the aggressive driving.

questions.question: If your vehicle is hydroplaning, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle hydroplanes, do not use the brakes. Instead, release the accelerator and push in the clutch. This will slow your vehicle and help it regain traction.

questions.question: The heavier a vehicle is:

options.text: The less important the brakes become.
The harder the brakes must work.
The quieter the brakes will sound.

questions.correctAnswerText: The harder the brakes must work.
questions.explanation: A heavier vehicle requires brakes to work harder to stop completely.

questions.question: How should you hold the steering wheel?

options.text: With one hand so you can eat or drink.
With one hand at a time, switching hands.

questions.correctAnswerText: With both hands.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands on opposite sides for proper vehicle control.

questions.question: Vehicles driving behind a truck:

options.text: May not be able to see objects in front of the truck.
Usually have a clear view of the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not be able to see objects in front of the truck.
questions.explanation: A truck can block the view of drivers behind it, preventing them from seeing hazards ahead. Flash your brakes to warn other drivers before you slow or stop.

questions.question: When driving long distances, you should stop every ____ to take a break.
questions.correctAnswerText: Two hours
questions.explanation: Stop at least once every two hours or every 100 miles to prevent driver fatigue on long trips.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, which action is not recommended?

options.text: Moving your vehicle to the side of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Leaving the scene
questions.explanation: After an accident, protect the area, call authorities, help injured people, collect information, and report the accident. Leaving the scene is illegal and can result in losing your license.

questions.question: When it is hard for others to see your vehicle at dawn or dusk, you can help by:

options.text: Waving an arm out the window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning your lights on.
questions.explanation: When visibility is low, turn on your headlights to low beam. If you cannot see others, they cannot see you.

questions.question: When carrying cargo, you should:

options.text: Check the load and securing devices within the first 50 miles.
Avoid using your mirrors to look behind your vehicle.
Hold a cell phone in your hand in case of an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the load and securing devices within the first 50 miles.
questions.explanation: Inspect cargo and securing devices before starting. Check them again within the first 50 miles, every three hours or 150 miles, and after every break.

questions.question: Air storage tanks:

options.text: Are not allowed on a vehicle.
Store compressed air for the brakes.
Should be drained after every trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Store compressed air for the brakes.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks in an air brake system hold compressed air for the brakes. The number and size of tanks vary by vehicle.

questions.question: When carrying a wide load, a driver should:

options.text: Get special permits and follow special rules, such as driving only at certain times.
Honk at other drivers to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get special permits and follow special rules, such as driving only at certain times.
questions.explanation: Loads that are too long, too wide, or too heavy need special permits. These loads may only be driven at certain times of the day.

questions.question: When adjusting your mirrors before a trip, what should you see?

options.text: No part of your vehicle in any mirror.
A small part of your vehicle in the mirrors.
More than half of your vehicle in each mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: A small part of your vehicle in the mirrors.
questions.explanation: Your mirrors should show a small part of your vehicle. This helps you judge where other vehicles are on the road.

questions.question: What must you know to determine if your vehicle can handle a load?

options.text: The tire rating for the front tires only.
The tire rating for the rear tires only.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle's suspension rating.
questions.explanation: You must know your vehicle's suspension rating. This tells you the maximum weight your vehicle can safely carry.

questions.question: During the driving test, what will the examiner score you on?

options.text: How quickly you arrive at your destination.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your general driving behavior.
questions.explanation: The examiner will score you on how you perform driving maneuvers and your overall driving behavior.

questions.question: What endorsement must you pass to transport hazardous materials?
questions.correctAnswerText: Hazardous materials
questions.explanation: You need a hazardous materials endorsement to drive any vehicle that carries hazardous materials.

questions.question: When stopping, how should you press the brake pedal?
questions.correctAnswerText: Press down gradually.
questions.explanation: Press the brake pedal down gradually. Control your pressure to bring your vehicle to a slow, safe stop.

questions.question: If you are convicted of a traffic violation, what must you do?

options.text: The state will inform your employer.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must tell your employer.
questions.explanation: You must notify your employer within 30 days of any traffic conviction. You must also notify your motor vehicle licensing agency within 30 days if the conviction happened in another state. Parking tickets do not count.

questions.question: Which is NOT a reason to change gears?

options.text: The speed of the vehicle next to you

questions.correctAnswerText: The speed of the vehicle next to you
questions.explanation: You should shift gears based on engine speed and road speed. Check your vehicle manual for the correct rpm range, and watch your speedometer for the right speed to shift. Other vehicles' speeds should not affect when you shift.

questions.question: A visual low pressure warning should activate before air pressure drops to which level?
questions.correctAnswerText: Between 55 and 75 psi
questions.explanation: The warning signal should activate before air pressure drops to between 55 and 75 psi. The signal can be a light, buzzer, or other alarm.

questions.question: Poisonous fumes can enter the cab from:

options.text: The wrong type of fuel being used.
A lack of oil in the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: A defective exhaust system.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is very dangerous. It allows poisonous fumes to enter the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: Why should you do pre-trip inspection steps in the same order each time?

options.text: You will be less likely to forget to check something.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will be less likely to forget to check something.
questions.explanation: Using the same order every time helps you remember all the important steps. You are less likely to skip something you need to check.
